newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani policeman suspected of Murtaza killing.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani policeman suspected of Murtaza killing.

text.p: Pakistani authorities on Sunday arrested a senior police officer accused of involvement in the killing of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza, police sources said.
They said senior superintendent Wajid Durrani was arrested after a complaint lodged with police accused him of conspiring Murtaza's alleged murder in a police shootout in Karachi on September 20.

Durrani was among several policemen named as accused in the complaint lodged on Saturday by Murtaza's breakaway faction of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party after a court order and was suspended after the shooting.
The police are searching for the other accused policemen and raided several possible hideouts, the sources said.

Murtaza was killed in what police called a crossfire with his guards. But his supporters disputed the report and sought the registration of their own parallel first information report with police, which was allowed by the Sindh High Court on Saturday.
Benazir Bhutto, dismissed by President Farooq Leghari five days ago on disputed charges of corruption and misrule, also said that Murtaza's killing was a conspiracy against her family and government.
